g.textArea: Plan previews changes; apply changes infrastructure. A branch name alone does not select dev, staging or production.

rect.data-content:
Phase 1: Development
Extend existing PR planning.
Pilot the controlled apply path.
Separate apply approval: team decision.

Phase 2: Staging
Add target-specific PR plans.
Explicit final-plan approval.
Apply and verify staging.

Phase 3: Production
Add target-specific PR plans.
Explicit final-plan approval.
Apply and verify production.

Decisions: affected roots and shared-module callers; required checks; reviewers; apply identity and trigger.
Dev gate policy, protected approval mechanism, plan freshness, and shared/common/RD scope remain to agree.

PR checks / plan failed
Author fixes change

1. Confirm baseline
Existing dev-only plan workflow
Required checks and reviewer rules
Current apply owner and identity

2. Agree controls
PR scope and module consumers
Per-target approvers and apply gate
Code / plan / state consistency

3. Pilot development
Enforce PR checks and review
Final plan + controlled apply
Record revision and outcome

4. Extend coverage
Staging then production plans
Explicit final-plan approval gates
Agree shared/common/RD scope

Required PR checks publish a plan for every affected in-scope root.
PR approval references current code; changed code requires renewed review.
Final plan matches the selected revision, root, inputs and current state.
Only authorized execution can apply; outcome and failures are traceable.

Team decisions
Confirm dev gate and staging/production approvers.
Choose supported approval mechanism and identities.
Agree pilot roots, ownership and completion criteria.

Plan each target against its own configuration and state.
Shared-module changes must identify affected consumer roots.
Shared/common/RD and protected foundation roots need explicit scope.
QA/lab provisioning remains a separate proposal.

Plan freshness
Merge order or infrastructure drift can alter the final plan.
Reject stale plans; re-plan and renew authorization.
Serialize conflicting applies to the same state.
